rapid_method.name: Rapid first pass
rapid_method.interpretation: Domain-level initial impressions based on current knowledge. They are not indicator scores, an evidence-led HDRL assessment or a benchmark.

rapid_questions.question: How consistently are the data needed for research available, linkable and kept up to date within this assessment boundary?
rapid_questions.consider: Consider coverage, refresh cycles, linkage, identifiers and whether data can move between the relevant services in routine practice—not only in a pilot.
rapid_questions.why: Research cannot be dependable when required data are incomplete, stale, hard to link or confined to disconnected services.

rapid_questions.question: How consistently can data be understood, quality-assessed and combined for pooled or federated analysis?
rapid_questions.consider: Consider terminology, metadata, quality monitoring, common data models, interoperability, curated datasets and reproducible definitions—not simply whether data can be accessed.
rapid_questions.why: Available data still create delay and risk when meaning, provenance, quality or interoperability are unclear.

rapid_questions.question: How clear, lawful, proportionate and predictable are the routes for approving and enabling research access?
rapid_questions.consider: Consider legal basis, access decisions, ethics, cross-border working, disclosure control, researcher accreditation and permissions as they operate in practice.
rapid_questions.why: Trusted research needs safeguards and decision routes that are understandable, proportionate and dependable—not governance documents alone.

rapid_questions.question: How well does the service support external researchers, cross-organisation collaboration and reproducible delivery?
rapid_questions.consider: Consider active users, support, research outputs, multi-site delivery, training, trials and appropriate commercial access.
rapid_questions.why: Readiness should be visible in dependable research delivery and user support, not infrastructure claims alone.

rapid_questions.question: How clearly does the service demonstrate transparency, public benefit and meaningful public involvement?
rapid_questions.consider: Consider public registers, accessible reporting, lay governance, opt-outs, engagement and independent learning or assurance.
rapid_questions.why: Trusted health-data research depends on legitimacy, useful transparency and evidence that public benefit shapes decisions.

rapid_questions.question: How resilient are the funding, operating model and evidence of value needed to sustain the service?
rapid_questions.consider: Consider funding horizon, financial risk, pricing, cost recovery, partnerships and credible evidence of value.
rapid_questions.why: Capability that cannot be maintained, staffed or funded is not dependable operating capacity.

rapid_questions.question: How well do workforce capacity, specialist skills, clear roles and service culture support dependable delivery?
rapid_questions.consider: Consider staffing headroom, defined responsibilities, specialist skills, retention, workforce planning and collaboration.
rapid_questions.why: A capable platform can still fail to deliver when specialist people, operating headroom or service behaviours are missing.

rapid_questions.question: How secure, usable, resilient and scalable is the technical environment under realistic demand?
rapid_questions.consider: Consider secure environments, user experience, compute, storage, security operations, privacy-enhancing technology and responsible AI.
rapid_questions.why: Technical readiness requires secure and supportable operation under realistic demand—not a one-off deployment.

impression_bands.label: Starting
impression_bands.description: Capability appears limited, fragmented or mainly informal.

impression_bands.label: Developing
impression_bands.description: Plans and early capability exist, but routine delivery appears uneven.

impression_bands.label: Defined
impression_bands.description: Responsibilities and processes appear documented and in regular use.

impression_bands.label: Managed
impression_bands.description: Performance appears measured, standardised and actively managed.

impression_bands.label: Continuously improving
impression_bands.description: Learning, comparison and improvement appear systematic and sustained.

A.common_mistake: Counting data that exist somewhere as research-ready without checking coverage, refresh, linkage permissions and routine delivery.
dependencies: C: lawful access and linkage governance
H: secure infrastructure and data flows

B.common_mistake: Treating a one-off mapping or data dictionary as evidence of consistently governed semantics, quality and interoperability.
dependencies: A: representative and current source data
H: metadata, model and pipeline tooling

C.common_mistake: Equating a written policy with an operating pathway that is understood, measured and used consistently.

D.common_mistake: Counting projects or publications without defining the denominator, period, service contribution or quality of support.
dependencies: A–C: usable data and workable governance
G: service and research support capacity

E.common_mistake: Treating one-way communications as meaningful involvement, or publication alone as evidence that transparency is useful.
dependencies: D: evidence of research use and benefit

F.common_mistake: Treating current funding as sustainability without testing renewal risk, cost recovery, demand and operating liabilities.

G.common_mistake: Counting posts rather than funded capacity, specialist competence, retention risk and headroom for real demand.
dependencies: D: user support and service demand

H.common_mistake: Treating certification, procurement or a successful pilot as evidence of secure, usable and scalable operation.

A: Dataset inventory with coverage, refresh and access information
Records of routine pooled or federated data use
B: Metadata catalogue or data dictionary with coverage information
Terminology or common-data-model mapping and validation records
Reusable dataset, phenotype or transformation documentation
C: Published access route, decision criteria and applicant guidance
Access, ethics or disclosure-control turnaround measures
Redacted decision, audit or mutual-recognition records
D: Service demand, project delivery and time-to-output measures
Researcher support standards and satisfaction findings
Records of multi-site, training, trial or partnership delivery
E: Public project register and accessible transparency reporting
Public-involvement membership, decisions and feedback loops
Complaints, opt-out, engagement or independent-learning records
F: Approved budget, funding agreement and forward financial plan
G: Workforce plan, funded establishment and vacancy measures
Skills matrix, role framework and development records
Turnover, retention, survey or succession evidence
Service standards, collaboration and knowledge-sharing records
H: User onboarding, accessibility or satisfaction measures
Certification, audit, penetration-test and remediation records
Backup, incident, security-operations, PET or responsible-AI evidence

evidence_guidance.provenance: Domain examples are de-identified patterns synthesised from the Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales HDRL applications. Indicator-specific ideas are drawn at runtime from the canonical catalogue's minimum-evidence wording.
evidence_guidance.caution: Examples are prompts, not a checklist, required evidence set or proof that a maturity level has been met. Evidence must match the stated assessment boundary and date.

recommendation_rules.when: A maturity judgement has no linked evidence record.
recommendation_rules.output: Treat the judgement as provisional and ask what document, metric, audit record or other source could substantiate it.

recommendation_rules.when: A response has low certainty or is not known.
recommendation_rules.output: Identify the person closest to this capability and the evidence needed to resolve the uncertainty.

recommendation_rules.when: An indicator has not been assessed.
recommendation_rules.output: Decide whether the indicator is relevant, who should review it and by when.

recommendation_rules.when: The assessor records an improvement note.
recommendation_rules.output: Carry the assessor's own proposed action into the report with a link back to the indicator; do not invent an action.

recommendation_rules.when: Independent team judgements span more than one adjacent maturity level or use different applicability statuses.
recommendation_rules.output: Review interpretation, scope and evidence before agreeing a consensus; do not average the responses.
